messages.subject: not recognizing WHERE on a column of class logical
messages.subject_clean: not recognizing WHERE on a column of class logical
messages.body_plain:
Hello, thank you so much for any help!

This works:

shallow_Dem_jur<-sqldf('
SELECT country,COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no) FROM sponge WHERE period="Jurassic" AND class_name="Demospongea"
GROUP BY country
')

shallow_Dem_jur
                 country COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no)
1                Algeria                             5
2              Argentina                             1
3                Austria                            17
4                 Canada                             7
5                  China                            29  #... etc

But this does not work:

shallow_Dem_jur<-sqldf('
SELECT country,COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no) FROM sponge_sql WHERE period="Jurassic" AND class_name="Demospongea" AND above_fair_wb="TRUE"
GROUP BY country
')

Nor does this:

shallow_Dem_jur<-sqldf('
SELECT country,COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no) FROM sponge_sql WHERE above_fair_wb="TRUE"
GROUP BY country
')

All I get is:

shallow_Dem_jur
[1] country                       COUNT(DISTINCT occurrence_no)
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

The only difference I can tell is that the columns period and class_name are of class character, but the column above_fair_wb is of class logical.

I tried to fix this with

class(sponge_sql[,77])<-as.character(sponge_sql[,77])

But the column is STILL logical.

How can I either fix the columns to be character class, or how do I properly frame a WHERE clause for logical vectors?

Thanks! This is day 3 of sqldf and it's working wonders but I'm still getting stuck hourly.

- Kathleen, a paleontologist

SQLite does not have a logical / boolean datatype.  TRUE will become 1 and FALSE will become 0.  For example,

> DF <- data.frame(a = 1:3, b = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
> sqldf("select * from DF where b = 0")
  a     b
1 3 FALSE
> sqldf("select * from DF where b = 1")
  a    b
1 1 TRUE
2 2 TRUE

The H2 database, which is also supported by sqldf, does have a boolean data type so with it we can do this:

> library(RH2)
Loading required package: RJDBC
Loading required package: rJava
> sqldf("select * from DF where b = 'TRUE'")
  a    b
1 1 TRUE
2 2 TRUE
> sqldf("select * from DF where b = 'FALSE'")
  a     b
1 3 FALSE

messages.subject: Merging by date results in C stack usage error
messages.subject_clean: Merging by date results in C stack usage error
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I recently noticed an error that occurs when I use sqldf to merge two dataframes by date.

Try this example code:

#======================================

g <- data.frame(date=as.Date(c("1927-01-31","1927-02-28")),x=c(2,3))
h <- data.frame(date=as.Date(c("1927-01-31","1927-02-28")),y=c(4,5))
final <- sqldf("select d1.*, d2.y from g d1 left join h d2 on d1.date=d2.date")

#======================================

Looks simple but if I execute it, it fails with the error "Error: C stack usage is too close to the limit."  If we do this in error=recover mode, we see a bunch of recursive calls to as.Date.numeric().

My session information:

R version 3.0.2 (2013-09-25)
Platform: x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu (64-bit)

attached base packages:
[1] tcltk     stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods
[8] base

other attached packages:
[1] sqldf_0.4-7           RSQLite.extfuns_0.0.1 RSQLite_0.11.4
[4] DBI_0.2-7             gsubfn_0.6-5          proto_0.3-10

This is a fresh install and I have not seen this error previously, so I'm thinking it might be a bug in a recent version of sqldf (or a related package).

Can anyone else reproduce it?

# ... now run your code ...

or else use svn to get the development version and build it from source.
